Hi David / team — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and the two asked-for items: a concise acceptance/playbook for the POC and a short sketch of performance vs cost tradeoffs so your infra and procurement can align.

Key points from the conversation:
- Goal: proof that Redwood inference can meet production latency and throughput targets for Pinion’s multi-turn summarization pipeline while keeping per-token cost within budget.
- Primary KPIs you called out: P50 latency < 80ms, P95 < 250ms, sustained throughput ~200 reqs/min (avg request size ~350 tokens), and inference cost target <= $0.0009/token.
- Success signals: qualitative accuracy (red team score / human eval) comparable to current baseline, <3% failure/error rate, and stable KV-cache behavior across session lengths.
- Ownership: Naomi (sales/ops) will own milestones; Aditya will own runtime/infra questions and sizing; Ben will coordinate success eval and CS handoff.

Next steps (short):
1) I’ll send an acceptance playbook with concrete measurement windows, roles, and timeline. (attachment: pinion_poc_scope.xlsx)
2) We’ll provide a cost/instance sketch and a recommended latency/quantization plan for your infra review. (attachment: redwood_poc_cost_estimate.pdf)
3) Procurement: if you can share your standard PO window and any required contract terms that would be helpful — Naomi will coordinate.

Proposed timeline: 6-week POC from kickoff (week 0: data handover & sandbox; week 1–3: initial runs and tuning; week 4: stress/throughput validation; week 5: human eval and acceptance run; week 6: decision & next steps).

I’ll follow with the detailed playbook in the next email. Thanks — Naomi

Hi all — attached is the playbook and a short cost sketch (two attachments). Below is the condensed acceptance & measurement plan — please review and flag anything missing.

POC Acceptance & Measurement Plan (condensed)
- Measurement windows: three 30-minute steady-state windows for throughput validation; three 5-minute windows for latency percentile measurement under representative traffic (interleaved request sizes to match your distribution).
- Latency targets: P50 < 80ms, P90 < 150ms, P95 < 250ms. Measurements taken at the gateway post-batching with live KV cache enabled.
- Throughput targets: baseline 200 reqs/min sustained, burst allowance to 350 reqs/min for short periods (<= 5 min) to simulate peak patterns.
- Cost target: effective inference cost <= $0.0009/token (this is after our suggested dynamic batching and int8 quantization on the model variant we plan to serve). If we hit higher token counts per request we’ll re-evaluate batching window.
- Quality targets: human-eval accept rate >= 85% on your standard rubric (we’ll run a 200-sample blind eval). Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) average >= 0.82 vs your internal gold set for summary fidelity. Error/failure rate < 3% (timeouts, OOMs, API errors).
- Rollback/fallback policy: if P95 latency exceeds 350ms for more than two windows or error rate >5% we’ll fallback to a conservative model variant and trigger a joint incident review that will pause acceptance.

Ops & ownership
- Naomi Feldman (Sales / Program): POC timeline, customer coordination, acceptance decision owner.
- Aditya Rao (Infra / Runtime): instance sizing, quantization profile, routing & batching configs, runbook for stress tests.
- Ben Carter (Customer Success): human eval orchestration, dataset ingestion support, post-POC handoff notes.

Deliverables (week-by-week)
- Week 0: Sandbox creds, sample payload spec, ingestion checklist.
- Week 1–2: Baseline runs + tuning (latency and token-cost optimization).
- Week 3–4: Throughput and stress validation windows + quantization validation.
- Week 5: Human eval & acceptance run (200 blind samples).
- Week 6: Readout and decision meeting.

Attachments: pinion_poc_scope.xlsx (detailed measurements, test scripts, contact list); redwood_poc_cost_estimate.pdf (instance choices, rough cost-per-hour and projection against your expected token volume).

Can procurement share PO cadence? We’ll produce an SOW draft if procurement wants one — Naomi will own contracting.

Thanks — Naomi

Adding a few technical notes from infra perspective so expectations align:
- Instance sizing: for the requested latencies at 350-token median we recommend a 2x A10G pool for initial runs, with an autoscale floor of 2 instances and a burst policy to add 1–2 replicas during stress windows. This keeps P95 headroom without overcommitting.
- Batching: we’ll use adaptive batching with a 15ms batching window; in our tests that preserves P50 while improving cost by ~22% on similar workloads.
- Quantization: int8 is our go-to for cost reduction; we’ll validate quality on a 200-sample holdout. If your business metric is sensitive to subtle token-level differences we can fallback to q4f16.
- Cost cap: the $0.0009/token target is achievable in the steady-state we discussed, assuming your request-token distribution stays near the stated mean (~350). If average tokens/request increases to 600+, expect ~30–40% higher cost per request unless we further tune batching or model size.

Request for Pinion: please share a 1,000-sample anonymized set (no PHI) representing typical conversations so we can pre-run the tuning and provide a narrower estimate by Monday. That will also let us pre-check for any edge-case memory pressure.

I’ll stand by to size the SOW hours once procurement confirms PO cadence.

—Aditya
